sources.title: Spatial Representations of Granule Cells and Mossy Cells of the Dentate Gyrus
sources.access: PMC open (abstract and metadata read; HTML full text blocked by reCAPTCHA)
sources.role: Primary: granule cell vs mossy cell firing pattern comparison, historical misidentification correction
sources.key_finding: Granule cells fire sparsely with single place fields; mossy cells fire promiscuously with multiple fields

sources.title: Hilar mossy cell degeneration causes transient dentate granule cell hyperexcitability and impaired pattern separation
sources.access: PMC open (abstract read; full text via PMC available but HTML blocked by reCAPTCHA)
sources.role: Primary: mossy cell ablation experiment proving net inhibitory effect
sources.key_finding: Selective mossy cell ablation → granule cell hyperexcitability → impaired contextual discrimination

sources.title: Re-evaluating Circuit Mechanisms Underlying Pattern Separation
sources.access: PMC open (abstract read; HTML full text blocked by reCAPTCHA)
sources.role: Theoretical framework: dimensionality as unified concept for pattern separation
sources.key_finding: Pattern separation is best understood as dimensionality expansion, not just sparsification

sources.title: Pattern separation in the hippocampus
sources.role: Review: comprehensive synthesis of pattern separation evidence across species and methods
sources.key_finding: Hippocampal DG is the main locus of pattern separation; aging and neurogenesis modulate capacity

sources.title: Sparse activity of identified dentate granule cells during spatial exploration
sources.role: Primary: direct in vivo quantification of granule cell sparsity with juxtacellular identification
sources.key_finding: Majority of morphologically identified granule cells are silent during exploration; active ones have single fields

sources.title: Adult neurogenesis in the mammalian hippocampus: Why the dentate gyrus?
sources.role: Review: DG sparse coding mechanism and adult neurogenesis functional role
sources.key_finding: Only 2-5% of granule cells activated per experience; adult neurogenesis modulates pattern separation capacity

sources.title: Paradox of Pattern Separation and Adult Neurogenesis: A Dual Role for New Neurons Balancing Memory Resolution and Robustness
sources.role: Review: dual/paradoxical role of adult-born GCs in pattern separation
sources.key_finding: Immature GCs enhance competition but also reduce representational stability; net effect depends on task parameters

sources.title: Recurrent Excitatory Feedback From Mossy Cells Enhances Sparsity and Pattern Separation in the Dentate Gyrus via Indirect Feedback Inhibition
sources.role: Computational model: mechanism by which mossy cells enhance pattern separation via feedback inhibition
sources.key_finding: Mossy cell excitation of interneurons → feedback inhibition of granule cells → enhanced sparsity and pattern separation

sources.title: Temporal pattern separation in hippocampal neurons through multiplexed neural codes
sources.role: Electrophysiology: multi-timescale pattern separation in granule cells
sources.key_finding: Granule cells separate patterns at <100ms (spike timing) and >100ms (rate) scales; both require GABAergic inhibition

sources.title: Contributions of adult neurogenesis to dentate gyrus network activity and computations
sources.role: Review: how adult-born GCs modulate DG network activity and pattern separation
sources.key_finding: Adult-born GCs generate feed-forward inhibition in CA3; differentially receive LEC vs MEC inputs

sources.title: Hilar mossy cell circuitry controlling dentate granule cell excitability
sources.role: Circuit analysis: dormant basket cell hypothesis
sources.key_finding: Mossy cell loss silences basket cells, disinhibiting granule cells; supports indirect inhibition mechanism

sources.title: A computational theory of hippocampal function, and empirical tests of the theory
sources.access: ABSTRACT ONLY — subscription journal, full text not read
sources.role: Background: foundational computational theory of DG pattern separation and CA3 pattern completion
sources.key_finding: DG performs pattern separation via sparse expansion coding; CA3 performs pattern completion via recurrent collaterals

sources.title: A novel, evolutionarily conserved inhibitory circuit selectively regulates dentate gyrus mossy cell function
sources.role: New finding: VGluT3+ interneurons selectively inhibit mossy cells (meta-inhibition circuit)
sources.key_finding: VGluT3+ interneurons target mossy cells specifically; evolutionarily conserved to primates; implies dedicated mossy cell control module
sources.caution: PREPRINT — single laboratory, requires independent replication and peer review
